locators.section: How Redis expires keys; replication link/AOF

primary_sources.independent_evidence_summary: The page distinguishes in-place mutation from replacement; GT rejects finite deadlines on persistent keys; non-positive expiry is deletion. GT history is 7.0.0. Passive/active expiry and replication semantics supply no service p99 measurement.

primary_sources.version: Live Redis command documentation; KEEPTTL introduced 6.0.0, applicable to 7.2
primary_sources.independent_evidence_summary: Ordinary successful SET replaces the value and drops its prior TTL; KEEPTTL preserves it. Later 8.4 conditions are outside the assessed command forms.

primary_sources.version: Live primary Redis documentation; relevant 7.2 event implementation separately checked
primary_sources.independent_evidence_summary: Notification delivery requires configuration and subscribers. E selects keyevent channels, g generic events, x expiry events. Del differs from expired; expiry-event delivery has no TTL-zero timing guarantee. Disconnection loses messages. The command list describes negative timeouts; zero is explicit in P1 and I1.

primary_sources.version: Redis upstream release tag 7.2.0; representative target-series implementation, not a service build attestation
primary_sources.independent_evidence_summary: GT returns zero when there is no existing expiry. An already-due explicit timeout deletes and generates del. EXPIRE uses seconds; PTTL uses a millisecond deadline minus a millisecond command-time snapshot.
primary_sources.method: public HTTPS retrieval; static text inspection only

locators.symbol: KEEPTTL parsing and expiration option exclusion

primary_sources.independent_evidence_summary: Unmet NX/XX returns before replacement. SET selects SETKEY_KEEPTTL for KEEPTTL; supplied expiration is assigned afterward. KEEPTTL parsing excludes explicit expiration options.
primary_sources.method: public HTTPS retrieval; static text inspection only

primary_sources.independent_evidence_summary: setKey removes the expiry unless SETKEY_KEEPTTL is selected. Ordinary expiration deletion generates expired, distinct from the explicit due-timeout branch in I1.
primary_sources.method: public HTTPS retrieval; static text inspection only

primary_sources.independent_evidence_summary: HSET obtains the hash object and updates fields in place; it does not replace the key through setKey or assign a new expiry. This corroborates P1.
primary_sources.method: public HTTPS retrieval; static text inspection only

claim_evidence.operation: Successful HSET field update on an existing, unexpired hash key
claim_evidence.conditions_exceptions: Existing key-level deadline is preserved, not refreshed; no existing TTL remains persistent. Replacement/recreation is outside this operation.
claim_evidence.corrected_wording_assessment: Appropriately bounded; no material correction needed.

claim_evidence.operation: Successful plain SET replacement without expiration option or KEEPTTL
claim_evidence.conditions_exceptions: Existing TTL is removed. Explicit expiration sets a deadline; KEEPTTL retains it. Unmet NX/XX does not replace. Successful replacement, rather than a mere syntactically valid command, governs the conclusion.
claim_evidence.corrected_wording_assessment: The replacement/persistent correction and conditional-command distinction are supported.

claim_evidence.operation: Successful SET key value KEEPTTL on the executing primary
claim_evidence.conditions_exceptions: Keeps an existing key deadline while value changes; does not attach a timeout to a persistent key. Does not establish replication durability or post-promotion service behavior.
claim_evidence.corrected_wording_assessment: Scope and remaining deployment uncertainty are appropriate.

claim_evidence.operation: EXPIRE key seconds GT, finite positive seconds on a persistent existing key
claim_evidence.conditions_exceptions: Persistent is infinite for GT, so condition skips with reply 0. GT extends a volatile key only for a strictly later deadline. Unconditional positive EXPIRE or NX can add a timeout to a persistent key.
claim_evidence.corrected_wording_assessment: Infinity/deadline correction and bounded alternatives are supported.

claim_evidence.operation: Successful unconditional EXPIRE key 0 on an existing key versus ordinary expiry deletion
claim_evidence.target: Redis OSS 7.2; event observation depends on notify-keyspace-events configuration
claim_evidence.conditions_exceptions: Zero causes logical deletion and del; ordinary expiration deletion generates expired. Default notifications are disabled. Configured subscribers can still lose Pub/Sub messages on disconnect. Immediate deletion is not a physical-memory cleanup latency claim.
claim_evidence.corrected_wording_assessment: Event distinction is correct. P3 alone describes negative timeouts; the zero boundary is independently supported by P1 and 7.2.0 code.

claim_evidence.operation: Service p99 expiry-to-cleanup latency under replica failover
claim_evidence.target: Redis OSS 7.2 service; no endpoint, benchmark, durability/retry/failover trace or cleanup definition supplied
claim_evidence.conditions_exceptions: Command availability and expiration precision are not evidence of a service p99 under failover. Background/passive expiry and notification delay distinguish deadline from observation. The candidate does not claim the target is impossible.
claim_evidence.corrected_wording_assessment: Unverified <25 ms p99 is the supported disposition; actual defined service measurements would resolve it.

limitations.finding: The candidate attributes the HSET-preservation passage to Refreshing expires. The passage is in the opening Description; Refreshing expires concerns calling EXPIRE again.
limitations.materiality: Correct URL and command semantics are preserved; the supporting passage is readily navigable. This is a locator defect, not an unsupported decision.

limitations.finding: The proposed PTTL check says decreases without specifying elapsed sampling time. Separate samples within the same millisecond can legitimately be equal. Positive/decreasing PTTL is also a coarse check of deadline preservation, rather than an exact deadline-equality oracle.
limitations.materiality: This is a brief prospective check with no executable harness or claimed result; it still discriminates dropped TTL from retained TTL. No execution requirement or new architecture is imposed. It is not a material source error or omission.
